entities.text: Mastipuram Ritesh Reddy, vs Union Of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
This Writ Petition is filed seeking to grant the following relief:
"... to issue a Writ, Order or Direction more particularly one in the nature of Writ of Mandamus declaring the action of respondent No.2 in not issuing the passport by keeping the application pending vide File No.HY1075423269523, dated 01.06.2023,
for reissuance of passport as illegal, arbitrary, violative of the principles of the natural justice, against the settled principles of law and also violative of Articles, 14, 19 and 21 of the Constitution of India, the Passport Act, 1967 and the principles of natural justice and consequently direct respondent No.2 to reissue the passport to the petitioner pursuant to the application, dated 01.06.2023, vide file No.HY1075423269523 forthwith and to pass such other order or orders as this Hon'ble Court may deem fit and proper in the circumstances of the case."
2.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri P. Devender, learned Standing Counsel for Central Government appearing for the respondents.
3. It is the case of the petitioner that he was holding a passport bearing No.Z4027817, issued by respondent No.2 on 27.01.2017 valid till 26.01.2027.

Since the petitioner shifted his residence to Ridhira Retreat, Survey No.388, Manchirevula, Gandipet, Ranga Reddy District, he made application, dated 01.06.2023, seeking reissuance of the passport by incorporating the present address and specifying the reasons as "change in the existing personal particulars - address".

The respondents, while taking steps for re-issuing the passport to the petitioner, called for a report from the concerned police and came to know about the pendency of a criminal case in C.C.No.324 of 2022 pending on the file of Additional Judicial First Class Magistrate at Vikarabad, Vikarabad District.

entities.text: Additional Judicial First Class Magistrate at Vikarabad, Vikarabad District
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: In view of pendency of the said criminal case, respondent No.2 kept the application of the petitioner pending for re-issuance of the passport to the petitioner.
Aggrieved by such action of respondent No.2, the petitioner approached this Court by filing the present writ petition.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner also placed reliance on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Vangala Kasturi Rangacharuyulu v. Central Bureau of Investigation1, wherein the provisions of the Passports Act, 1967 (for short, 'the Act, 1967') were examined, pending criminal cases against the applicants, and held that a passport can be refused only in case 2020 Crl.L.J. (SC) 572 where the applicant is convicted during the period of five years immediately preceding the date of application for an offence involving moral turpitude and sentence for imprisonment for not less than two years.
Section 6 (2) (f) of the Act, 1967 relates to a situation where the applicant is facing trial in a criminal Court.

sentences.text: The sentence was reduced to a period of one year.
The petitioner therein had approached the Hon'ble Apex Court by way of filing an appeal and the same is pending.
Therefore, considering the said facts, the Hon'ble Apex Court held that the Passport Authority cannot refuse renewal of the passport on the ground of pendency of the criminal appeal.
Thus, the Hon'ble Apex Court directed the Passport Authority to renew the passport of the applicant without raising the objection relating to the pendency of the aforesaid criminal appeal.

5. Sri P. Devender, learned Standing Counsel for Central Government appearing for respondents Nos.1 and 2, submitted that the re-issue/renewal of the passport cannot be issued to the applicant,
in case, if any criminal cases are pending against the said applicant.

He further submitted that said issue is dealt with by the learned Single Judge of this Court in the case of Pervez Mohammad Abdul v. Union of India and another2 and the issue of re-issue of the passport be governed by the very same judgment.

entities.text: Pervez Mohammad Abdul v. Union of India and another2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6. On the other hand, learned counsel for the petitioner contended that renewal of the passport is different from issuance of fresh passport.
He further submitted that the petitioner shifted his residence and therefore, he intended to change his residential addressed in the passport.

7. This Court, having considered the submissions made on either side and after perusing the material on record including the judgment in the case of Pervez Mohammad Abdul (supra), is of the considered view that in the light of Section 6 of the Passport Act, 1967, the re-issue of passport is also governed by the very same provisions and restrictions as are applicable for issuing a fresh passport or renewal of the passport.
Admittedly, a criminal case is pending against the petitioner herein before the competent Court.

Therefore, this Court is 2023(1) ALD 394 (TS) of the considered view that application of the petitioner can be directed to be considered by imposing restrictions and conditions as were imposed in the case of Pervez Mohammad Abdul.

iv) On filing such an application, the Passport Officer/Authority shall consider the same afresh in the light of the observations made by this Court herein as well as the contents of the undertaking given by the petitioner for renewal of his passport in accordance with law, within three (3) weeks from the date of said application; and v) On renewal of the Passport, the petitioner herein shall deposit the original renewed passport before the trial Court in C.C.No.324 of 2022 pending on the file of Additional Judicial First Class Magistrate at Vikarabad, Vikarabad District.
vi) However, liberty is granted to the petitioner herein to file petition before the trial Court in the aforesaid calendar case seeking permission to travel abroad.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous applications, if any pending, shall also stand closed.
